summary: Twenty-four capabilities, split by the physics being solved and then by problem class. The mechanics branches follow the NAFEMS PSE technical areas (structural analysis, material behaviour, fatigue and fracture, CFD, multibody, electromagnetics, acoustics, multiphysics, optimisation and probabilistic analysis); process simulation follows the CAPE-OPEN component classes, power systems the IEEE PES committee areas, and validation the ASME V&V family. O*NET's Analytical, CAD and Industrial control categories added fire, naval architecture, nuclear transport and building-performance capabilities the seeds lacked.

capabilities.name: Structural finite element analysis
capabilities.definition: Given a part or assembly idealized as solids, shells or beams with materials, loads and constraints, compute displacements, stresses, natural frequencies, dynamic response and stability limits.

crosswalk.label: V&V 10: verification and validation in computational solid mechanics

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Structural finite element analysis (linear, nonlinear, dynamics, fatigue, composites)'. Split along the NAFEMS groups: this node keeps the Structural Analysis group (linear, dynamics, buckling, thermo-mechanical, geometric nonlinearity and contact); material models and composites moved to simulate.material_behavior; fatigue and fracture to simulate.fatigue_fracture.

tasks.name: Linear static stress analysis
tasks.definition: Given an elastic body under small-displacement loads and constraints, compute displacement, strain and stress fields.
tasks.inputs: geometry or mesh; linear elastic materials; loads; constraints
tasks.outputs: displacement, strain and stress fields; reaction forces
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS LE1-LE11 linear elastic benchmarks have reference solutions

tasks.name: Normal modes analysis
tasks.definition: Given a structure's stiffness, mass and constraints, compute its natural frequencies and mode shapes.
tasks.inputs: mesh; materials with density; constraints; optional prestress
tasks.outputs: natural frequencies; mode shapes; modal effective mass
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS free-vibration (FV) benchmarks have reference frequencies

tasks.name: Harmonic, random and spectrum response
tasks.definition: Given a linear structure and frequency-domain or shock-spectrum excitation, compute steady-state response amplitudes, power spectral densities or peak responses.
tasks.inputs: mesh or modal model; damping; harmonic loads, base PSD or response spectrum
tasks.outputs: frequency response functions; RMS and peak stresses and displacements
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS forced-vibration benchmarks have reference responses

tasks.name: Implicit transient dynamic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a structure with time-varying loads and initial conditions, integrate the equations of motion in time to obtain the response history.
tasks.inputs: mesh; materials; damping; load histories; initial conditions
tasks.outputs: displacement, velocity, acceleration and stress histories
onet_products: Automatic dynamic incremental nonlinear analysis ADINA
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS transient dynamics benchmarks and closed-form single-degree-of-freedom solutions

tasks.name: Linear eigenvalue buckling
tasks.definition: Given a structure under a reference load, compute the critical load multipliers and buckled mode shapes.
tasks.inputs: mesh; materials; reference loads; constraints
tasks.outputs: buckling load factors; buckling mode shapes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: closed-form Euler column, plate and cylinder buckling solutions

tasks.name: Thermal stress analysis
tasks.definition: Given a temperature field and thermo-elastic material properties, compute the resulting thermal strains, stresses and distortion.
tasks.inputs: mesh; temperature field or thermal loads; expansion coefficients; constraints
tasks.outputs: thermal displacement and stress fields
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS thermo-mechanical benchmarks and closed-form thick-cylinder solutions

tasks.name: Large deformation and contact analysis
tasks.definition: Given a structure with large displacements, follower loads or contacting surfaces, solve the nonlinear equilibrium path including contact pressures and post-buckling.
tasks.inputs: mesh; materials; contact pairs and friction; load steps
tasks.outputs: load-displacement path; contact pressure and status; post-buckled shape
onet_products: Automatic dynamic incremental nonlinear analysis ADINA
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS geometric nonlinear and contact benchmarks (Hertz contact has a closed form)

tasks.name: Explicit impact and crash simulation
tasks.definition: Given a structure, impact or blast conditions and rate-dependent materials, integrate short-duration highly nonlinear dynamics to predict deformation, energy absorption and failure.
tasks.inputs: mesh; rate-dependent materials with failure; initial velocities, impacts or blast loads; contact definitions
tasks.outputs: deformation history; energy balance; accelerations; failed elements
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Taylor bar impact and public vehicle crash models with test data exist, but no shared scored suite

capabilities.name: Material nonlinearity and composites
capabilities.definition: Given a structure and constitutive data for metals, polymers, elastomers or laminated composites, compute inelastic and anisotropic response, ply stresses and failure.
capabilities.notes: New node from the NAFEMS Material Behaviour group; absorbs the composites part of the first seed. Composite panel sizing sits here because its core is ply-level failure.

tasks.name: Elastic-plastic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a metallic structure and a plasticity model with hardening, compute plastic strains, residual stresses and collapse loads.
tasks.inputs: mesh; yield surface and hardening data; load history
tasks.outputs: plastic strain and residual stress fields; limit load
onet_products: Automatic dynamic incremental nonlinear analysis ADINA
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS plasticity benchmarks and closed-form thick-cylinder autofrettage solutions

tasks.name: Elastomer and hyperelastic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a rubber or soft-material part and test-fitted hyperelastic parameters, compute large-strain deformation and stresses.
tasks.inputs: mesh; hyperelastic constants or test curves; loads and contact
tasks.outputs: deformed shape; stretch and stress fields; force-deflection curve
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: homogeneous-deformation tests have closed forms, but part-level references are scarce

tasks.name: Creep and viscoelastic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a structure at load and temperature over time and a creep or viscoelastic law, compute time-dependent strain, relaxation and rupture life.
tasks.inputs: mesh; creep law or Prony series; load and temperature history
tasks.outputs: creep strain and stress relaxation over time; creep damage
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: NAFEMS creep benchmarks exist; component-level validation data are limited

tasks.name: Laminate stress and ply failure
tasks.definition: Given a layup, ply properties and in-plane and bending loads, compute ply stresses and first-ply and last-ply failure envelopes.
tasks.inputs: ply properties; stacking sequence; force and moment resultants
tasks.outputs: ply stresses and strains; failure indices; failure envelopes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the World-Wide Failure Exercises (WWFE-I to III) give test data for blind prediction

tasks.name: Composite progressive damage
tasks.definition: Given a composite structure and damage-initiation and evolution laws, predict delamination, matrix cracking and residual strength.
tasks.inputs: mesh with plies and cohesive interfaces; damage parameters; loads
tasks.outputs: damage fields; delamination growth; strength and stiffness loss
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: WWFE-III and open-hole coupon data exist, but scatter is large

tasks.name: Aerospace panel sizing
tasks.definition: Given internal loads on stiffened panels and allowables, choose layups and stiffener dimensions that satisfy all failure modes at least weight.
tasks.inputs: panel loads from a global model; material allowables; candidate concepts
tasks.outputs: panel sizes and layups; margins of safety by failure mode
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: classical stiffened-panel test cases exist, but the sizing objective is design-specific

tasks.name: Multiscale homogenization
tasks.definition: Given a representative volume of a heterogeneous material, compute its effective macroscopic properties.
tasks.inputs: unit cell geometry; constituent properties; periodic boundary conditions
tasks.outputs: effective stiffness, conductivity or strength
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Hashin-Shtrikman bounds and published unit-cell results give references

capabilities.name: Fatigue and fracture analysis
capabilities.definition: Given stress or strain histories and cracks or flaws in a component, predict fatigue life, crack growth and fracture or flaw acceptability.
capabilities.notes: Split from the first seed to follow NAFEMS, which treats Fatigue and Flaw Assessment as separate areas from structural analysis.

tasks.name: Stress-life and strain-life fatigue
tasks.definition: Given stress or strain histories at critical locations and material S-N or strain-life curves, compute cumulative damage and fatigue life.
tasks.inputs: stress results or load histories; S-N or epsilon-N curves; surface factors
tasks.outputs: damage and life contours; critical locations
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SAE Fatigue Design and Evaluation keyhole specimen test programs give measured lives

tasks.name: Fatigue crack growth
tasks.definition: Given an initial crack, geometry, load spectrum and crack-growth law, compute crack length versus cycles and remaining life.
tasks.inputs: crack geometry; stress intensity solution; load spectrum; da/dN data
tasks.outputs: crack length versus cycles; inspection intervals
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: published constant- and variable-amplitude test data exist; no maintained scored suite

tasks.name: Fracture parameter computation
tasks.definition: Given a cracked body, compute stress intensity factors, J-integral or energy release rate along the crack front.
tasks.inputs: mesh with crack front; materials; loads
tasks.outputs: K, J or G along the crack front; crack-tip fields
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: handbook stress intensity solutions (Tada, Murakami) give references

tasks.name: Fitness-for-service flaw assessment
tasks.definition: Given a detected flaw, component geometry, stresses and toughness, assess acceptability against a failure assessment diagram.
tasks.inputs: flaw dimensions; component geometry; primary and secondary stresses; toughness
tasks.outputs: failure assessment point; acceptability; critical flaw size
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 example problem manual gives worked results

tasks.name: Welded joint fatigue
tasks.definition: Given welded joint geometry and stresses, compute hot-spot or structural stresses and life against weld classification curves.
tasks.inputs: weld geometry; nominal or hot-spot stresses; detail category
tasks.outputs: weld fatigue damage and life
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: IIW recommendations include worked examples; part-level data are sparse

capabilities.name: Structural frame analysis and code checking
capabilities.definition: Given a building, bridge, offshore or piping structure as members and connections with code-defined loads, compute member forces and check them against design codes.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Engineering

capabilities.notes: Was the first half of seed 'Structural frame analysis and design-code checking; geotechnical analysis'. Geotechnics split out because its inputs (soil models) and benchmarks differ. Pipe stress sits here because it is beam-element analysis judged against a piping code.

tasks.name: Linear frame analysis
tasks.definition: Given a frame or truss of members, sections, supports and load cases, compute member forces, deflections and reactions.
tasks.inputs: member geometry; sections; releases; load cases and combinations
tasks.outputs: member forces and moments; deflections; reactions
onet_products: Oasys structural design and analysis software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: textbook and AISC design example frames have closed-form answers

tasks.name: Member design code checking
tasks.definition: Given member forces and sections, check steel, concrete, timber or masonry members against a design code and report utilization.
tasks.inputs: member forces; section and material grades; design code and options
tasks.outputs: utilization ratios; governing clauses; required sizes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: AISC and ACI design example manuals give worked results

tasks.name: Concrete slab and post-tensioned floor analysis
tasks.definition: Given a slab layout, supports, tendons and loads, compute moments, deflections and reinforcement or tendon requirements.
tasks.inputs: slab geometry; columns and walls; tendon profiles; loads
tasks.outputs: moment and deflection fields; reinforcement and tendon design
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Post-Tensioning Institute and code design examples exist

tasks.name: Seismic structural analysis
tasks.definition: Given a structural model and ground motions or response spectra, compute seismic demands by spectrum, pushover or nonlinear time-history analysis.
tasks.inputs: structural model; mass; spectra or ground-motion records; hysteretic models
tasks.outputs: drifts, base shear, member demands; capacity curves
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: FEMA P-751 design examples and shake-table blind-prediction contests give references

tasks.name: Bridge load analysis and rating
tasks.definition: Given a bridge model and design or rating vehicles, compute moving-load envelopes and load ratings.
tasks.inputs: girder or grillage model; lanes; vehicle loads; code factors
tasks.outputs: force envelopes; influence lines; rating factors
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: FHWA steel and prestressed-concrete bridge design examples give worked results

tasks.name: Offshore structure analysis
tasks.definition: Given a fixed offshore structure and metocean conditions, compute wave and current loads, member stresses and joint code checks.
tasks.inputs: jacket or topside model; wave, current and wind data; soil springs
tasks.outputs: member and joint utilizations; in-place and fatigue results
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: API RP 2A examples exist, but public full-structure references are scarce

tasks.name: Piping stress analysis
tasks.definition: Given a piping layout, supports, temperatures and pressures, compute pipe stresses, support loads and nozzle loads and check them against a piping code.
tasks.inputs: pipe routing; supports; operating conditions; piping code
tasks.outputs: code stress ratios; support and nozzle loads; displacements
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NRC piping benchmark problems (NUREG/CR-1677) give reference solutions

capabilities.name: Geotechnical analysis
capabilities.definition: Given soil or rock stratigraphy, properties and an engineered structure such as a slope, foundation, pile, pavement or excavation, compute stability, seepage, settlement and soil-structure response.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Engineering

capabilities.notes: Second half of seed 'Structural frame analysis and design-code checking; geotechnical analysis'. No source taxonomy in the brief covers geotechnics; nodes follow standard practice areas. Natural groundwater flow stays with earth; seepage through engineered earthworks is here.

tasks.name: Slope stability analysis
tasks.definition: Given a slope or embankment section, soil strengths and pore pressures, find the critical slip surface and factor of safety.
tasks.inputs: cross-section; soil strengths; pore pressures; loads
tasks.outputs: critical slip surface; factor of safety
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the ACADS slope stability verification problems have referee answers

tasks.name: Seepage through earthworks
tasks.definition: Given a dam, levee or excavation section with permeabilities and water levels, compute pore pressures, flow rates and exit gradients.
tasks.inputs: section; hydraulic conductivity functions; boundary heads
tasks.outputs: pore pressure field; seepage flux; exit gradients
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: analytical flow-net and Dupuit solutions give references

tasks.name: Consolidation and settlement
tasks.definition: Given a foundation load on compressible soils, compute immediate and consolidation settlement over time.
tasks.inputs: soil profile; compressibility and consolidation parameters; loads
tasks.outputs: settlement versus time; excess pore pressure
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Terzaghi one-dimensional and Mandel consolidation problems have closed forms

tasks.name: Pile driving and capacity analysis
tasks.definition: Given a pile, hammer and soil model, or measured driving signals, predict drivability and stresses or back-calculate pile capacity by wave-equation analysis.
tasks.inputs: pile and hammer properties; soil resistance model; or force and velocity records
tasks.outputs: blow count versus capacity; driving stresses; capacity estimate
onet_products: GRL Engineers Wave Equation Analysis Program GRLWEAP
Pile Dynamics Case Pile Wave Analysis Program CAPWAP
Pile Dynamics Pile Driving Analyzer PDA
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: dynamic predictions can be scored against static load tests, but data sets are proprietary

tasks.name: Finite element soil-structure interaction
tasks.definition: Given an excavation, tunnel, foundation or retaining structure in soil with constitutive models and construction stages, compute deformations and structural forces.
tasks.inputs: staged geometry; soil constitutive parameters; structural elements
tasks.outputs: ground deformation; wall or lining forces; stage-by-stage safety
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: German Geotechnical Society numerical benchmark exercises show wide scatter between users

tasks.name: Rock mechanics for underground openings
tasks.definition: Given an underground opening or mine layout, rock-mass properties and in-situ stresses, compute stresses, pillar loads and support requirements.
tasks.inputs: mine or tunnel layout; rock-mass properties; in-situ stress
tasks.outputs: stress and convergence fields; pillar safety factors; support design
onet_products: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health LaModel
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Kirsch circular-opening solution is closed form; field cases are site-specific

tasks.name: Pavement structural response
tasks.definition: Given pavement layers, materials, traffic and climate, compute layer stresses and strains and predict distress over the design life.
tasks.inputs: layer thicknesses and moduli; traffic spectra; climate
tasks.outputs: critical strains; predicted cracking, rutting and roughness
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: layered-elastic solutions are closed form; distress models are calibrated empirically

capabilities.name: Computational fluid dynamics
capabilities.definition: Given a flow domain, fluid properties and boundary conditions, solve the flow equations for velocity, pressure, turbulence, species and phase fields and derived forces.

crosswalk.label: V&V 20: verification and validation in computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer
Computing methodologies > Modeling and simulation > Simulation types and techniques > Continuous simulation

capabilities.notes: Seed 'Computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer' split three ways: flow here, thermal analysis (including lumped thermal networks that are not CFD) in simulate.thermal, and fire and smoke in simulate.fire. Tasks are split by flow regime because each has its own benchmark community.

tasks.name: Internal incompressible flow
tasks.definition: Given a duct, valve, manifold or vessel geometry and inlet and outlet conditions, compute the velocity and pressure fields and pressure losses.
tasks.inputs: fluid domain; fluid properties; inlet and outlet conditions; turbulence model
tasks.outputs: velocity and pressure fields; pressure drop; flow distribution
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ERCOFTAC classic collection cases (backward-facing step, pipe flows) have measured data

tasks.name: External aerodynamics
tasks.definition: Given a vehicle or body shape and freestream conditions, compute the surrounding flow and the lift, drag and moments.
tasks.inputs: surface geometry; freestream Mach, Reynolds and attitude
tasks.outputs: force and moment coefficients; surface pressure; wake
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: AIAA Drag Prediction and High Lift Prediction Workshops publish test cases and comparisons

tasks.name: High-speed compressible flow
tasks.definition: Given a geometry and transonic, supersonic or hypersonic conditions, compute shock structures, heating and loads.
tasks.inputs: geometry; freestream state; gas model
tasks.outputs: shock positions; pressure and heat-flux distributions; loads
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource verification and validation cases

tasks.name: Turbomachinery flow
tasks.definition: Given blade-row geometry, rotational speed and inlet and outlet conditions, compute stage performance and flow fields.
tasks.inputs: blade geometry; rotor speed; inlet total conditions; back pressure
tasks.outputs: pressure ratio; efficiency map; blade loading
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NASA Rotor 37 and Rotor 67 have measured data and blind-test histories

tasks.name: Multiphase and free-surface flow
tasks.definition: Given a domain with two or more phases, compute interface motion, phase fractions and resulting loads.
tasks.inputs: domain; phase properties; initial interface or inlet fractions
tasks.outputs: phase distribution over time; interface position; loads
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SPHERIC benchmark cases and the dam-break experiments have measured data

tasks.name: Reacting flow and combustion
tasks.definition: Given a combustor or burner geometry, fuel and oxidizer streams and a chemistry model, compute flame structure, temperatures and emissions.
tasks.inputs: geometry; inlet compositions; reaction mechanism; turbulence-chemistry model
tasks.outputs: temperature and species fields; heat release; pollutant emissions
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TNF Workshop flames (Sandia flame D and others) have measured data

tasks.name: Wind flow around buildings
tasks.definition: Given buildings or structures and an atmospheric boundary-layer inflow, compute wind pressures, pedestrian-level wind and dispersion near structures.
tasks.inputs: building geometry; inflow wind profile and direction
tasks.outputs: surface pressure coefficients; pedestrian wind speeds
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Architectural Institute of Japan benchmark cases and the CEDVAL wind-tunnel data sets
tasks.notes: Natural atmosphere over terrain belongs to earth; this task is flow around designed structures.

capabilities.name: Heat transfer and thermal analysis
capabilities.definition: Given a part, assembly or spacecraft with thermal properties, heat loads and boundary conditions, compute temperatures and heat flows by conduction, convection and radiation.

crosswalk.label: V&V 20: verification and validation in computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer

capabilities.notes: Split from seed 'Computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer': lumped thermal network solvers and radiation-exchange codes are a separate function from CFD and have their own product lineage (SINDA, ESATAN, TRASYS).

tasks.name: Conduction heat transfer analysis
tasks.definition: Given a solid's geometry, conductivity and thermal boundary conditions, compute steady or transient temperature fields.
tasks.inputs: mesh; conductivity, density and specific heat; heat loads and boundary conditions
tasks.outputs: temperature fields over time; heat fluxes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NAFEMS thermal benchmarks and closed-form conduction solutions

tasks.name: Lumped thermal network analysis
tasks.definition: Given a system idealized as thermal nodes and conductors with heat sources, solve for node temperatures and heat flows over time.
tasks.inputs: nodes; conductors; capacitances; heat loads; boundary temperatures
tasks.outputs: node temperature histories; heat flows
onet_products: K&K Associates Thermal Analysis Kit TAK
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: analytical network cases verify solvers; system models are proprietary

tasks.name: Radiation exchange and orbital heating
tasks.definition: Given surface geometry, optical properties and an orbit or environment, compute view factors, radiative couplings and absorbed solar, albedo and planetary fluxes.
tasks.inputs: surface model; emissivity and absorptivity; orbit and attitude
tasks.outputs: view factors; radiative conductors; absorbed heat flux histories
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: analytical view-factor catalogues give exact references

tasks.name: Electronics cooling analysis
tasks.definition: Given a board, enclosure or package layout with component powers and cooling, compute component and junction temperatures.
tasks.inputs: board and enclosure geometry; component powers; fans and heat sinks
tasks.outputs: junction and board temperatures; airflow; thermal margins
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: JEDEC JESD51 package test conditions are standard, but benchmark models are vendor-held

tasks.name: Conjugate heat transfer
tasks.definition: Given coupled fluid and solid domains, solve fluid flow and solid conduction together to obtain wall temperatures and heat-transfer rates.
tasks.inputs: fluid and solid domains; properties; flow and thermal boundary conditions
tasks.outputs: temperature fields in fluid and solid; heat-transfer coefficients
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ASME V&V 20 example problems and heated-channel data sets

tasks.name: Heat exchanger rating and design
tasks.definition: Given heat-exchanger type, geometry and stream conditions, compute duty, outlet temperatures and pressure drops, or size the exchanger for a required duty.
tasks.inputs: exchanger type and geometry; stream flows, temperatures and properties
tasks.outputs: duty; outlet temperatures; pressure drops; required area
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: effectiveness-NTU closed forms; industrial rating correlations are proprietary

tasks.name: Insulation and heat-loss calculation
tasks.definition: Given pipe, duct or equipment surfaces, insulation and ambient conditions, compute heat loss, surface temperature and economic insulation thickness.
tasks.inputs: surface geometry; insulation type and thickness; process and ambient temperatures
tasks.outputs: heat loss; surface temperature; economic thickness
onet_products: North American Insulation Manufacturers Association NAIMA 3E Plus
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ASTM C680 procedures give deterministic reference results

capabilities.name: Fire and smoke simulation
capabilities.definition: Given an enclosure or building, fuel and fire scenarios, compute fire growth, smoke and heat movement, detector and sprinkler response, structural heating and occupant egress.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Engineering

capabilities.notes: New capability. The original 'cfd' function held fire CFD and zone models; O*NET lists over two dozen fire-protection engineering tools, and performance-based fire design is a distinct function with its own V&V literature. No source taxonomy in the brief has a fire node. Wildland fire spread is natural and belongs to earth.

tasks.name: Zone fire modeling
tasks.definition: Given compartments, vents and a heat release rate, compute upper-layer temperature, layer height and species over time with a two-zone model.
tasks.inputs: compartment geometry; vents; heat release rate; materials
tasks.outputs: layer temperatures and heights; species concentrations over time
onet_products: Consolidated Model of Fire and Smoke Transport CFAST
Consolidated fire and smoke transport model CFAST
Fire Protection Engineering Tools FPETool software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NUREG-1824 verification and validation of fire models gives measured experiments

tasks.name: Field fire modeling
tasks.definition: Given a 3D enclosure, fuels and ignition, solve low-Mach reacting flow to compute temperature, smoke and toxic gas fields.
tasks.inputs: 3D geometry; fuel properties; ignition and heat release; ventilation
tasks.outputs: temperature, velocity, visibility and species fields
onet_products: Simulation of fires in enclosures SOFIE software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the FDS Verification and Validation Guides compare against dozens of experiments

tasks.name: Detector and sprinkler activation
tasks.definition: Given a fire growth curve, ceiling geometry and device response properties, compute the time to detector, sprinkler or vent activation.
tasks.inputs: heat release rate curve; ceiling height and spacing; response time index
tasks.outputs: activation times; heat release at activation
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: ceiling-jet correlations are closed form; activation test data exist in NIST reports

tasks.name: Smoke control system analysis
tasks.definition: Given a building's flow paths, fans and stack effect, compute pressure differences and smoke movement for a smoke management design.
tasks.inputs: building flow network; leakage areas; fans; temperatures
tasks.outputs: pressure differences across barriers; airflow rates; smoke spread
onet_products: Analysis of Smoke Control Systems ASCOS
Atria smoke management engineering tools ASMET
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: network airflow cases verify solvers; system tests are building-specific

tasks.name: Structural fire response
tasks.definition: Given fire exposure and structural members, compute member temperatures and the resulting loss of strength and stability.
tasks.inputs: member geometry; thermal and mechanical properties at temperature; fire exposure curve
tasks.outputs: temperature histories; deflections; time to failure
onet_products: Fire Response of Structures Thermal FIRES-T software
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: ISO 834 furnace tests and the Cardington tests provide data

tasks.name: Window breakage and fire spread
tasks.definition: Given a compartment fire and glazing properties, predict when windows break and the resulting change in ventilation.
tasks.inputs: glass properties; fire exposure; frame shading
tasks.outputs: time to glass breakage
onet_products: Berkeley Algorithm for Breaking Window Glass in a Compartment Fire BREAK1
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: small-scale breakage experiments exist

tasks.name: Egress and evacuation simulation
tasks.definition: Given a building layout, occupant population and behaviors, compute required safe egress times and congestion.
tasks.inputs: floor plans; exits; occupant numbers and profiles; pre-movement times
tasks.outputs: evacuation times; flow rates; congestion locations
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IMO MSC.1/Circ.1533 verification tests are used to compare evacuation models

tasks.name: Fire risk assessment
tasks.definition: Given a building, fire scenarios with frequencies and protection systems, compute expected risk to life by combining fire, smoke and egress models over scenarios.
tasks.inputs: scenario set with probabilities; building and protection data
tasks.outputs: expected life risk; fire cost expectation
tasks.benchmarkable: no: results depend on scenario weights with no ground truth

capabilities.name: Multibody dynamics and mechanisms
capabilities.definition: Given bodies connected by joints, forces and contacts, compute motions, joint reactions and interaction forces of mechanisms, machines, robots and human bodies.
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Multibody dynamics and mechanism kinematics'. Added granular (discrete element) flow, contact-rich robot simulation and human-body biomechanics, which O*NET lists and which use the same equations. Robot offline programming stays with produce.

tasks.name: Mechanism kinematic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a linkage or cam mechanism and input motions, compute positions, velocities and accelerations of all members and check interference.
tasks.inputs: bodies; joints; driver motions
tasks.outputs: position, velocity and acceleration histories; interference
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: closed-form four-bar and slider-crank solutions

tasks.name: Rigid multibody dynamics
tasks.definition: Given rigid bodies, joints, forces and initial conditions, integrate the equations of motion to compute motions and joint reactions.
tasks.inputs: masses and inertias; joints; force elements; initial state
tasks.outputs: motion histories; joint reaction forces; energy
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the IFToMM library of computational benchmark problems for multibody dynamics

tasks.name: Flexible multibody dynamics
tasks.definition: Given a mechanism with deformable members represented by modal or nodal flexibility, compute coupled large motion and elastic deformation.
tasks.inputs: multibody model; flexible body reductions or meshes; loads
tasks.outputs: motions; elastic deformations; dynamic stresses
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IFToMM benchmarks include flexible cases (for example the flexible slider-crank)

tasks.name: Granular flow by discrete elements
tasks.definition: Given particle shapes and contact laws and a container, chute or mill geometry, simulate bulk material flow and forces on equipment.
tasks.inputs: particle size, shape and contact parameters; equipment geometry and motion
tasks.outputs: flow patterns; mass flow rates; wall forces and wear
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: published DEM benchmark tests check contact models; calibration dominates real cases
tasks.notes: No O*NET product; included because bulk-handling equipment design depends on it.

tasks.name: Belt conveyor dynamic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a belt conveyor profile, belt, drives and material loading, compute belt tensions, power and starting and stopping transients.
tasks.inputs: conveyor profile; belt properties; drives and take-ups; material flow
tasks.outputs: tension distribution; drive power; transient tensions
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: CEMA design method gives reference steady-state tensions

tasks.name: Robot and grasp physics simulation
tasks.definition: Given a robot model, objects and contact properties, simulate contact-rich motion and evaluate grasp quality or controller behavior.
tasks.inputs: robot description; object geometry and mass; contact and friction; controller
tasks.outputs: trajectories; contact forces; grasp quality metrics
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: grasp and manipulation benchmarks exist (YCB object set), but scoring mixes control and physics

tasks.name: Human body biomechanics
tasks.definition: Given a posture or motion, anthropometry and external loads, compute joint loads, muscle forces and strength capability of the human body.
tasks.inputs: body segment model; posture or motion capture; external forces
tasks.outputs: joint moments and compressive forces; muscle forces; percent capable
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Grand Challenge Competition to Predict In Vivo Knee Loads gives measured joint forces
tasks.notes: Workplace ergonomic assessment programs belong to operate; this task is the mechanics.

capabilities.name: Vehicle and vessel performance
capabilities.definition: Given a ship, aircraft, spacecraft or road vehicle and its operating environment, compute its stability, resistance, motions, trajectory or energy use.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Aerospace
Resistance; Propulsion; Seakeeping; Stability in Waves

capabilities.notes: New capability not in the seeds. O*NET lists a naval architecture cluster (stability, resistance, mooring), orbit analysis, drive-cycle and collision reconstruction tools that compute the physics of whole vehicles rather than parts. Vehicle and vessel operation (dispatch, dynamic positioning, flight planning) stays with move.

tasks.name: Ship hydrostatics and stability
tasks.definition: Given a hull form, compartments and loading, compute hydrostatics, intact and damaged stability and compliance with stability criteria.
tasks.inputs: hull offsets; compartments; weights and tank loads; damage cases
tasks.outputs: hydrostatic tables; righting-arm curves; criteria compliance
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: IMO intact stability criteria are deterministic, but reference hull sets are not public

tasks.name: Ship resistance and propulsion
tasks.definition: Given hull particulars and propulsor data, predict calm-water resistance, propulsor performance and required power versus speed.
tasks.inputs: hull form or parameters; propeller geometry; speed range
tasks.outputs: resistance and effective power curves; propeller efficiency; delivered power
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Gothenburg and Tokyo CFD workshops (KCS, KVLCC2, DTMB 5415) have towing-tank data

tasks.name: Seakeeping and wave loads
tasks.definition: Given a floating body and sea states, compute wave-induced motions, loads and response statistics.
tasks.inputs: hull or panel mesh; mass properties; wave spectra
tasks.outputs: response amplitude operators; motion statistics; wave loads
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ITTC seakeeping data and the IEA Wind OC3 to OC6 floating-platform code comparisons

tasks.name: Mooring analysis
tasks.definition: Given a moored vessel, lines, fenders and environmental loads, compute line tensions and vessel offsets.
tasks.inputs: vessel data; line and fender properties; wind, current and wave loads
tasks.outputs: line tensions; vessel excursions; safety factors
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: OC-series floating-wind comparisons include moorings; terminal cases are proprietary

tasks.name: Powertrain and drive-cycle simulation
tasks.definition: Given vehicle, engine or motor, transmission and battery models, simulate a drive cycle to compute fuel or energy use, emissions and performance.
tasks.inputs: vehicle parameters; powertrain component maps; drive cycle
tasks.outputs: fuel or energy consumption; emissions; acceleration and gradeability
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: certification cycles are standard, but vehicle models are proprietary

tasks.name: Flight and projectile trajectory
tasks.definition: Given an aircraft, missile or projectile with aerodynamic and mass data, simulate six- or three-degree-of-freedom flight through the atmosphere.
tasks.inputs: aerodynamic coefficients; mass properties; propulsion; atmosphere and initial state
tasks.outputs: trajectory; attitude; flight performance
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NASA six-degree-of-freedom flight simulation check-cases have reference trajectories

tasks.name: Orbit propagation and mission analysis
tasks.definition: Given orbital elements, force models and maneuvers, propagate spacecraft orbits and compute access, coverage and maneuver costs.
tasks.inputs: initial orbit state; gravity, drag and third-body models; maneuvers
tasks.outputs: ephemerides; access windows; delta-v budgets
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: published SGP4 verification vectors and GMAT-STK cross-comparisons give references

tasks.name: Vehicle collision reconstruction
tasks.definition: Given crash damage, rest positions and vehicle data, reconstruct impact speeds and trajectories by momentum, crush-energy or simulation methods.
tasks.inputs: vehicle masses and stiffness; crush profiles; scene measurements
tasks.outputs: impact speeds and delta-v; pre- and post-impact trajectories
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: staged collision tests (RICSAC) give measured speeds for scoring

capabilities.name: Electromagnetic field simulation
capabilities.definition: Given conductors, magnetic and dielectric materials, sources and boundaries, solve Maxwell's equations for static, low-frequency or full-wave fields and derived forces, losses and radiation.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Physics

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Electromagnetic field simulation (low and high frequency), optics'. Optics split out (lens and photonic design are a different practice). Signal integrity and microwave circuit simulation handed to design per the boundary table.

tasks.name: Low-frequency magnetic field analysis
tasks.definition: Given magnetic materials, coils and permanent magnets, compute static or eddy-current magnetic fields, forces, inductances and losses.
tasks.inputs: geometry; B-H curves and conductivities; coil currents or circuits; motion
tasks.outputs: flux density; forces and torques; inductance; eddy and core losses
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: COMPUMAG TEAM workshop problems have measured reference data

tasks.name: Electrostatic and quasi-static field analysis
tasks.definition: Given conductors at potentials and dielectrics, compute electric fields, capacitances and field stress on insulation.
tasks.inputs: geometry; permittivities and conductivities; potentials or charges
tasks.outputs: potential and field distributions; capacitance matrix; peak field stress
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: analytical capacitor and sphere-gap solutions give references

tasks.name: Electric machine performance
tasks.definition: Given motor, generator or transformer geometry, windings and materials, compute torque, back-EMF, efficiency maps and losses.
tasks.inputs: machine cross-section or 3D geometry; windings; materials; operating points
tasks.outputs: torque-speed and efficiency maps; losses; cogging torque
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: TEAM problem 30 (induction motor) gives reference torque

tasks.name: High-frequency full-wave analysis
tasks.definition: Given antennas, waveguides, components or scatterers, solve full-wave Maxwell's equations to compute S-parameters, radiation patterns and scattering.
tasks.inputs: geometry; materials; ports or incident waves; frequency band
tasks.outputs: S-parameters; field distributions; radiation patterns; radar cross-section
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Austin RCS benchmark suite and IEEE Std 1597.2 validation problems

tasks.name: Electromagnetic compatibility and exposure
tasks.definition: Given a device, enclosure or body model and sources, compute shielding, coupling, emissions or specific absorption rate.
tasks.inputs: device and enclosure geometry; cables; sources; tissue models
tasks.outputs: shielding effectiveness; coupled currents; SAR distributions
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEC/IEEE 62704-1 SAR benchmark models and IEEE Std 1597.2 problems

tasks.name: Radio propagation and coverage prediction
tasks.definition: Given transmitter sites, antennas and terrain, compute path loss and predicted coverage.
tasks.inputs: transmitter parameters; antenna patterns; terrain and clutter data
tasks.outputs: path loss; coverage maps; link margins
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ITU-R Study Group 3 measurement databanks

tasks.name: Charged particle beam simulation
tasks.definition: Given electrodes, magnets and particle sources, track charged particles through fields to compute beam trajectories, optics and space-charge effects.
tasks.inputs: field maps or geometry; particle source distribution
tasks.outputs: trajectories; beam envelopes; emittance; current deposition
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: analytic beam-optics cases check solvers; device data are proprietary

capabilities.name: Optical and photonic simulation
capabilities.definition: Given lenses, mirrors, sources, waveguides or nanostructures, compute light propagation by ray tracing or wave optics and derive image quality, illumination or mode and transmission properties.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Physics

capabilities.notes: Split from seed 'Electromagnetic field simulation (low and high frequency), optics' because ray-based optical design and photonic mode solving are separate practices with their own tools. No source taxonomy in the brief has an optics node.

tasks.name: Imaging optical system design
tasks.definition: Given a lens or mirror prescription and field and wavelength specifications, trace rays to compute aberrations and image quality and optimize the prescription.
tasks.inputs: surface prescriptions; materials; fields; wavelengths; merit function
tasks.outputs: spot diagrams; MTF; wavefront error; optimized prescription
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: reference ray traces for published prescriptions verify tracers; design quality is open-ended

tasks.name: Illumination and stray light analysis
tasks.definition: Given sources, optics and mechanical surfaces with scatter properties, trace non-sequential rays to compute illuminance, intensity and stray light.
tasks.inputs: source models; optical and mechanical geometry; surface scatter properties
tasks.outputs: illuminance and intensity maps; stray-light paths; efficiency
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: CIE 171:2006 includes test cases; scatter models limit accuracy

tasks.name: Waveguide mode solving and propagation
tasks.definition: Given a waveguide or fiber cross-section and indices, compute guided modes and propagate fields along the structure.
tasks.inputs: cross-section geometry; refractive indices; wavelength
tasks.outputs: mode profiles; effective indices; propagation loss and coupling
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: slab and step-index fiber modes have analytic solutions

tasks.name: Nanophotonic full-wave simulation
tasks.definition: Given a nanostructured or photonic-crystal device, solve Maxwell's equations in the time or frequency domain to compute transmission, reflection and band structure.
tasks.inputs: device geometry; dispersive materials; sources and monitors
tasks.outputs: transmission and reflection spectra; band diagrams; near fields
onet_products: Finite difference time domain FDTD software
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Mie scattering and photonic-crystal band structures have exact references

tasks.name: Thin-film and multilayer optics
tasks.definition: Given a stack of thin layers with complex indices, compute reflectance, transmittance and absorption versus wavelength and angle.
tasks.inputs: layer thicknesses; complex refractive indices; wavelengths and angles
tasks.outputs: reflectance, transmittance and absorptance spectra
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: transfer-matrix results are exact

tasks.name: Photonic integrated circuit and laser simulation
tasks.definition: Given a photonic circuit of lasers, modulators, waveguides and detectors, simulate time- or frequency-domain optical and electrical signals.
tasks.inputs: component models; circuit topology; drive signals
tasks.outputs: optical spectra and waveforms; eye diagrams; laser dynamics
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: laser rate-equation solutions verify solvers; component models are foundry-specific

tasks.name: Physical optics and adaptive optics simulation
tasks.definition: Given an optical system, atmospheric turbulence and a wavefront sensing and correction scheme, propagate wavefronts and compute corrected image quality.
tasks.inputs: pupil and optics model; turbulence profile; sensor and deformable mirror models
tasks.outputs: residual wavefront error; Strehl ratio; point-spread functions
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: diffraction-limited cases are exact; AO system results depend on configuration

capabilities.name: Acoustics, noise and vibration
capabilities.definition: Given a structure, enclosure, room or outdoor site with sound or vibration sources, compute sound fields, transmission, noise levels and vibration response, or identify modal properties from tests.
capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Acoustics, vibration and noise'. Structural forced response stays in simulate.structural_fea; this node holds the acoustic side and test-based modal identification.

tasks.name: Vibro-acoustic finite and boundary element analysis
tasks.definition: Given a vibrating structure and an interior or exterior fluid domain, compute sound pressure fields, radiated power and transmission.
tasks.inputs: structural and acoustic meshes; material and fluid properties; excitations
tasks.outputs: sound pressure fields; radiated power; transfer functions
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the EAA computational acoustics benchmark platform publishes reference cases

tasks.name: Statistical energy analysis
tasks.definition: Given a system divided into subsystems with coupling and damping loss factors, compute high-frequency energy distribution and noise levels.
tasks.inputs: subsystem definitions; loss factors; input powers
tasks.outputs: subsystem energies; sound and vibration levels by band
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: two-subsystem analytic cases verify solvers; vehicle data are proprietary

tasks.name: Outdoor sound propagation
tasks.definition: Given noise sources, terrain, buildings and barriers, compute sound levels at receivers by standard propagation methods.
tasks.inputs: source sound power; terrain and buildings; ground and meteorology
tasks.outputs: receiver levels; noise maps; barrier attenuation
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ISO/TR 17534-3 gives quality-assurance test cases for ISO 9613-2 implementations

tasks.name: Room acoustics simulation
tasks.definition: Given a room geometry, surface absorption and sources, compute impulse responses and acoustic parameters such as reverberation time and clarity.
tasks.inputs: room geometry; absorption and scattering coefficients; source and receiver positions
tasks.outputs: impulse responses; reverberation time; clarity and speech indices
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: PTB round robins and the BRAS database give measured rooms
tasks.notes: No O*NET product; included because architectural acousticians rely on it.

tasks.name: Loudspeaker and enclosure modeling
tasks.definition: Given driver parameters, enclosure and crossover design, compute frequency response, excursion and impedance.
tasks.inputs: Thiele-Small parameters; enclosure volume and ports; crossover components
tasks.outputs: frequency response; cone excursion; impedance
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: lumped-parameter closed-form responses

tasks.name: Experimental modal analysis
tasks.definition: Given measured frequency response functions or operating responses, identify natural frequencies, damping and mode shapes.
tasks.inputs: measured FRFs or response time histories; sensor geometry
tasks.outputs: identified frequencies, damping ratios and mode shapes
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: the GARTEUR SM-AG19 testbed provides shared measured data

capabilities.name: Coupled multiphysics simulation
capabilities.definition: Given a device whose behavior depends on interacting physics, solve the coupled fluid, structural, thermal, electrical or electrochemical fields together.

crosswalk.label: Computing methodologies > Modeling and simulation > Simulation types and techniques > Multiscale systems

capabilities.notes: New capability from the NAFEMS Multiphysics area. Holds problems where no single-physics node can stand alone. Semiconductor device and process (TCAD) simulation was left with design because the original 'ic' function owns it.

tasks.name: Fluid-structure interaction
tasks.definition: Given a flexible structure in a flow, solve coupled fluid and structural dynamics to compute deformation, loads and flutter or vortex-induced vibration.
tasks.inputs: fluid and structural models; coupling interface; flow conditions
tasks.outputs: coupled deformation and flow histories; loads; stability
onet_products: Automatic dynamic incremental nonlinear analysis ADINA
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Turek-Hron FSI benchmark has reference values

tasks.name: Microelectromechanical device simulation
tasks.definition: Given a micro-device layout, process stack and drive conditions, compute coupled electrostatic, mechanical and damping behavior.
tasks.inputs: layout and process stack; materials; drive voltages
tasks.outputs: displacements; capacitance; resonance; pull-in voltage
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: parallel-plate pull-in has a closed form; device data are proprietary

tasks.name: Electro-thermal-mechanical coupling
tasks.definition: Given conductors, piezoelectric or thermoelectric materials and electrical loads, compute coupled Joule heating, temperature, stress and electrical response.
tasks.inputs: geometry; coupled material properties; electrical and thermal loads
tasks.outputs: current density; temperature; stress; electrical response
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: analytic coupled cases exist; few shared device benchmarks

tasks.name: Battery and fuel cell modeling
tasks.definition: Given cell geometry, electrochemical parameters and load cycles, compute voltage, current distribution, temperature and degradation.
tasks.inputs: electrode and electrolyte parameters; cell geometry; current or power profile
tasks.outputs: voltage curves; concentration and temperature fields; capacity fade
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Doyle-Fuller-Newman reference parameter sets allow code comparison; aging data vary

capabilities.name: Semiconductor process and device simulation
capabilities.definition: Given a fabrication recipe or a device structure, compute the resulting doping and geometry and the device's electrical behavior from carrier transport physics.
capabilities.notes: Added by the editor. The design author handed TCAD to simulate and the simulate author handed it to design, so it had no node. It is physics solving, so it sits here; compact-model extraction from its results stays in design.circuit_simulation. No counterpart was found in the listed source taxonomies, so the crosswalk is empty.

tasks.name: Semiconductor process simulation
tasks.definition: Given a starting wafer and a sequence of implant, diffusion, oxidation, deposition and etch steps, compute dopant profiles and the resulting device geometry.
tasks.inputs: wafer material and orientation; process step sequence with doses, energies, temperatures and times; mask layout
tasks.outputs: dopant concentration profiles; layer thicknesses; device cross-section geometry
onet_products: FLorida Object Oriented Process Simulator FLOOPS
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: measured dopant depth profiles for standard implants and anneals are published; production recipes are proprietary

tasks.name: Semiconductor device simulation
tasks.definition: Given a device structure with doping and applied biases, solve the coupled electrostatic and carrier transport equations for currents, capacitances and internal fields.
tasks.inputs: device geometry and doping; material and mobility models; bias conditions
tasks.outputs: current-voltage and capacitance-voltage curves; potential, field and carrier distributions
onet_products: FLorida Object Oriented Design Simulator FLOODS
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the ideal diode and the MOS capacitor have closed-form solutions, and measured curves for reference devices are published

tasks.name: Optical lithography simulation
tasks.definition: Given a mask pattern, illumination settings and a resist stack, compute the aerial image and the developed resist profile.
tasks.inputs: mask layout; illumination source and projection optics; resist and film stack
tasks.outputs: aerial image intensity; resist profile; process window
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: mask-optimization contests publish optical models and test layouts; resist models are proprietary
tasks.notes: The correction of layouts using such models is design.ic_signoff.

capabilities.name: Manufacturing process simulation
capabilities.definition: Given a part, tooling and process parameters, simulate a forming, casting, molding, joining, additive or machining process to predict defects, residual stress and final shape.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Engineering

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Manufacturing process simulation (casting, molding, forming, welding)'. Added additive manufacturing, machining and heat treatment. Shop-floor process monitoring (shot monitors) belongs to produce.

tasks.name: Casting fill and solidification
tasks.definition: Given a casting and gating design, alloy and process conditions, simulate mold filling and solidification to predict porosity, shrinkage and microstructure.
tasks.inputs: casting and mold geometry; alloy properties; pouring conditions
tasks.outputs: fill sequence; solidification times; porosity and shrinkage risk
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Sirrell-Campbell sand-casting benchmark has measured results

tasks.name: Injection molding simulation
tasks.definition: Given a plastic part, gates, cooling and process settings, simulate filling, packing and cooling to predict weld lines, sink and warpage.
tasks.inputs: part and runner geometry; polymer data; process settings
tasks.outputs: fill pattern; pressures; shrinkage and warpage
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: standard test moldings exist, but material data dominate errors
tasks.notes: No O*NET product in the assigned categories; injection molding is a large simulation market.

tasks.name: Sheet metal forming simulation
tasks.definition: Given a blank, die surfaces and press conditions, simulate forming to predict thinning, splits, wrinkles and springback.
tasks.inputs: blank and die geometry; sheet material model; binder and press parameters
tasks.outputs: thickness and strain distributions; forming limit margins; springback
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NUMISHEET benchmark problems have measured results

tasks.name: Forging and extrusion simulation
tasks.definition: Given a billet, dies and process conditions, simulate bulk deformation to predict material flow, die fill, loads and defects.
tasks.inputs: billet and die geometry; flow stress data; temperatures and speeds
tasks.outputs: material flow; forming loads; laps and underfill
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: ring-compression and published forging tests verify friction and flow

tasks.name: Welding distortion and residual stress
tasks.definition: Given a weld joint, heat source and sequence, simulate thermal and mechanical history to predict distortion and residual stress.
tasks.inputs: joint geometry; heat source parameters; weld sequence; temperature-dependent properties
tasks.outputs: temperature history; distortion; residual stress
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NeT Task Group 1 single bead-on-plate round robin has measured residual stresses

tasks.name: Additive manufacturing process simulation
tasks.definition: Given a part, build orientation, supports and process parameters, simulate the build to predict distortion, residual stress and melt-pool behavior.
tasks.inputs: part and supports; layer and scan parameters; material
tasks.outputs: distortion; residual stress; melt-pool size; compensated geometry
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NIST AM-Bench challenge problems have measured results

tasks.name: Metal cutting process simulation
tasks.definition: Given tool geometry, workpiece material and cutting parameters, predict cutting forces, temperatures, chip formation and tool wear.
tasks.inputs: tool geometry; workpiece flow stress; cutting speed, feed and depth
tasks.outputs: cutting forces; tool temperature; chip shape; wear
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: CIRP cutting-model comparisons exist; results vary with friction assumptions

tasks.name: Heat treatment and quenching simulation
tasks.definition: Given a part, steel grade and heat-treatment schedule, predict phase transformations, hardness, distortion and residual stress.
tasks.inputs: part geometry; alloy transformation data; heating and quench schedule
tasks.outputs: phase fractions; hardness; distortion; residual stress
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: Jominy end-quench tests give reference hardness

capabilities.name: Chemical process simulation
capabilities.definition: Given chemical components, thermodynamic models, unit operations and stream connections, compute heat and material balances, phase behavior and equipment performance of a process.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Physical sciences and engineering > Chemistry

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Chemical process flowsheeting, thermodynamics and reactor or separation design'. Tasks follow the CAPE-OPEN component classes (thermodynamics, unit operations, reactions) plus heat integration and power-cycle heat balance, which O*NET lists. Operator training simulators belong to produce.

tasks.name: Physical property and phase equilibrium
tasks.definition: Given a mixture composition, temperature and pressure and a property method, compute phase split, densities, enthalpies and transport properties.
tasks.inputs: components; property method and parameters; state conditions
tasks.outputs: phase fractions and compositions; thermodynamic and transport properties
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IAPWS-IF97 verification tables and NIST ThermoML experimental data

tasks.name: Computational thermochemistry
tasks.definition: Given elements, species databases, temperature and pressure, minimize Gibbs energy to compute equilibrium phases and compositions, including high-temperature and metallurgical systems.
tasks.inputs: species and solution databases; elemental amounts; temperature and pressure
tasks.outputs: equilibrium phases and amounts; phase diagrams; heat balances
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: NIST-JANAF tables and assessed phase diagrams give references

tasks.name: Steady-state flowsheet simulation
tasks.definition: Given feeds, unit operations and recycle connections, solve the plant heat and material balance.
tasks.inputs: feed streams; unit models and specifications; property method; topology
tasks.outputs: stream tables; equipment duties; converged recycles
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: textbook flowsheets (for example Williams-Otto) have known answers; no maintained scored suite

tasks.name: Dynamic process simulation
tasks.definition: Given a flowsheet with holdups, equipment sizes and controllers, integrate plant behavior through disturbances, startups and shutdowns.
tasks.inputs: flowsheet with holdups and sizes; control loops; disturbance scenarios
tasks.outputs: time histories of flows, levels, pressures and compositions
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: the Tennessee Eastman challenge process is a shared reference plant

tasks.name: Reactor modeling and kinetics
tasks.definition: Given a reaction mechanism with rate laws and a reactor type, compute conversion, selectivity and temperature profiles.
tasks.inputs: reaction mechanism and rate constants; reactor type and size; feeds
tasks.outputs: conversion and selectivity; concentration and temperature profiles
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: textbook reactor problems have closed forms; industrial kinetics are proprietary

tasks.name: Distillation and absorption column design
tasks.definition: Given feeds, column configuration and specifications, compute stage-by-stage compositions, duties and column sizing.
tasks.inputs: feed streams; stages and feed locations; specifications; property method
tasks.outputs: stage profiles; condenser and reboiler duties; tray or packing sizing
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: published column test cases exist; no scored suite

tasks.name: Batch and bioprocess simulation
tasks.definition: Given a recipe of batch steps or a fermentation and purification train, compute material balances, cycle times and equipment utilization.
tasks.inputs: batch recipe or unit procedures; equipment; feeds; kinetics
tasks.outputs: material balance per batch; cycle times; throughput and bottlenecks
tasks.benchmarkable: no: results depend on recipe assumptions with no public reference set

tasks.name: Agitated vessel and mixing design
tasks.definition: Given a stirred vessel, impeller and fluid properties, compute power draw, blend time, heat transfer and suspension.
tasks.inputs: vessel and impeller geometry; fluid properties; speed
tasks.outputs: power number and draw; blend time; heat-transfer coefficient
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: power-number correlations and published mixing experiments give references

tasks.name: Heat integration and pinch analysis
tasks.definition: Given hot and cold process streams, compute minimum utility targets and design a heat-exchanger network.
tasks.inputs: stream supply and target temperatures; heat capacities; minimum approach
tasks.outputs: composite curves; utility targets; exchanger network
onet_products: Thermal Analysis Systems The Energy Analyst
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: textbook pinch problems have exact utility targets

tasks.name: Power plant heat balance
tasks.definition: Given a thermal power cycle of turbines, boilers, heaters and condensers, compute the heat balance, heat rate and off-design performance.
tasks.inputs: cycle topology; component characteristics; ambient and load conditions
tasks.outputs: heat and mass balance; heat rate; output
onet_products: Fleet Asset Management and Optimization Solutions FAMOS PEPSE
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: textbook Rankine and Brayton cycles are exact; plant models are proprietary

capabilities.name: Power system analysis
capabilities.definition: Given an electrical network of generators, lines, transformers, loads and protection, compute power flows, fault currents, protection behavior, stability and transients.

crosswalk.label: Analytic Methods for Power Systems Committee
Power System Relaying and Control Committee

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Power system analysis (load flow, short circuit, protection, stability)'. Tasks follow IEEE PES committee areas. Real-time grid operations (EMS, DMS, OMS, SCADA, substation automation) belong to operate.

tasks.name: Transmission load flow and contingency
tasks.definition: Given a balanced network model with generation and load, solve bus voltages and branch flows and screen outage contingencies.
tasks.inputs: bus-branch model; generator dispatch; loads; contingency list
tasks.outputs: bus voltages and angles; branch flows; violations under contingencies

crosswalk.label: Analytic Methods for Power Systems Committee

onet_products: GE Energy Positive Sequence Load Flow Software PSLF
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEEE test cases and PGLib-OPF give reference networks and solutions

tasks.name: Unbalanced distribution feeder analysis
tasks.definition: Given a multi-phase distribution feeder with loads and distributed generation, solve unbalanced flows over time and assess hosting capacity.
tasks.inputs: three-phase feeder model; load and generation profiles
tasks.outputs: phase voltages and currents; losses; hosting capacity
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEEE PES distribution test feeders have reference results

tasks.name: Short-circuit analysis
tasks.definition: Given a network with source and equipment impedances, compute fault currents for symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults and check equipment duty.
tasks.inputs: network impedances; source contributions; fault locations and types; standard
tasks.outputs: fault currents; equipment interrupting duty
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEC TR 60909-4 gives example networks with reference fault currents

tasks.name: Protection coordination
tasks.definition: Given relays, fuses and breakers with their curves and network fault currents, select settings so devices operate selectively.
tasks.inputs: device time-current curves; fault currents; settings
tasks.outputs: coordination plots; settings; miscoordination flags

crosswalk.label: Power System Relaying and Control Committee

tasks.benchmarkable: partly: IEEE Std 242 examples exist; selectivity criteria vary by practice

tasks.name: Arc flash hazard analysis
tasks.definition: Given a facility network and protective device clearing times, compute incident energy and arc flash boundaries at equipment.
tasks.inputs: network model; fault currents; device clearing times; working distances
tasks.outputs: incident energy; arc flash boundary; labels
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEEE 1584 provides equations and worked examples

tasks.name: Transient and small-signal stability
tasks.definition: Given a network with machine, control and load dynamic models, simulate disturbances to assess rotor-angle, voltage and frequency stability.
tasks.inputs: network; dynamic models of machines, exciters, governors and inverters; disturbances
tasks.outputs: angle, voltage and frequency trajectories; damping; stability margins
onet_products: GE Energy Positive Sequence Load Flow Software PSLF
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEEE PES task-force benchmark systems (Kundur two-area, IEEE 39-bus) have reference responses

tasks.name: Electromagnetic transient simulation
tasks.definition: Given detailed network, converter and equipment models, simulate fast transients from switching, faults and lightning.
tasks.inputs: detailed component models; switching events; time step
tasks.outputs: instantaneous voltage and current waveforms; overvoltages
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: CIGRE HVDC benchmark system and IEEE switching examples

tasks.name: Harmonic analysis
tasks.definition: Given a network and nonlinear loads or converters, compute harmonic voltages and currents, distortion indices and resonances.
tasks.inputs: network model; harmonic source spectra; frequency scan range
tasks.outputs: harmonic voltage and current spectra; THD; resonance frequencies
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEEE harmonics modeling task-force test systems have reference results

tasks.name: Conductor sizing and voltage drop
tasks.definition: Given building or site circuits, loads and conductor options, compute voltage drop and select conductor and conduit sizes to code.
tasks.inputs: circuit lengths; loads; conductor types; code tables
tasks.outputs: voltage drop; conductor and conduit sizes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: National Electrical Code examples give reference sizes

tasks.name: Power electronic converter simulation
tasks.definition: Given a converter topology, switches, passive components and control, simulate switching waveforms, losses and control response.
tasks.inputs: converter schematic; device models; control scheme
tasks.outputs: voltage and current waveforms; losses; efficiency; ripple
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: ideal-switch converter waveforms have closed forms; device loss models are vendor-specific

tasks.name: Generation and transmission expansion planning
tasks.definition: Given demand forecasts, resource options, costs and policies, compute least-cost build-out of generation, storage and transmission over decades.
tasks.inputs: demand and resource data; technology costs; policy constraints
tasks.outputs: capacity build schedule; dispatch; costs and emissions
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: model intercomparisons exist, but there is no ground truth for future build-out

capabilities.name: Renewable energy system performance
capabilities.definition: Given a wind, solar or hybrid energy installation and resource data, compute energy yield, losses and component loads, and size systems to meet demand.

crosswalk.label: Energy Development and Power Generation Committee

capabilities.notes: New capability carved from the original 'power' function, whose patterns already listed PV, wind and hybrid tools. Energy yield from resource data is a different calculation from grid analysis. Resource mapping itself belongs to earth.

tasks.name: Photovoltaic energy yield
tasks.definition: Given PV array layout, modules, inverters, shading and weather data, compute hourly energy output and loss breakdown.
tasks.inputs: array layout; module and inverter data; horizon and near shading; weather file
tasks.outputs: hourly and annual energy; loss diagram; performance ratio
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: Sandia PV Performance Modeling Collaborative blind modeling comparisons

tasks.name: Wind farm energy yield and wakes
tasks.definition: Given turbine positions, power curves and wind climate, compute wake losses and annual energy production.
tasks.inputs: turbine layout; power and thrust curves; wind climate statistics; terrain
tasks.outputs: wake losses; annual energy production; uncertainty
onet_products: Risoe National Laboratory Wind Atlas Analysis and Application Program WAsP
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEA Wind Task 31 (Wakebench) and Horns Rev wake measurements

tasks.name: Wind turbine aeroelastic loads
tasks.definition: Given a turbine's blades, tower, controller and wind fields, simulate coupled aero-servo-elastic response to compute loads and power.
tasks.inputs: blade and tower structural and aerodynamic data; controller; turbulent wind fields
tasks.outputs: load time series; fatigue equivalent loads; power
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: IEA Wind OC3 to OC6 code comparison projects
tasks.notes: No O*NET product; included because it is the core design calculation for turbines.

tasks.name: Concentrating solar optics and performance
tasks.definition: Given heliostat or trough fields, receivers and solar data, trace sunlight to compute flux, optical efficiency and plant output.
tasks.inputs: collector field layout; mirror and receiver geometry; sun shape; weather
tasks.outputs: flux maps; optical efficiency; annual output
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: SolarPACES guidelines and ray-tracing intercomparisons exist

tasks.name: Hybrid and microgrid system sizing
tasks.definition: Given loads, renewable resources, storage, generators and costs, simulate dispatch over a year and select the least-cost system configuration.
tasks.inputs: load profile; resource data; component costs and characteristics
tasks.outputs: optimal component sizes; dispatch; cost of energy
onet_products: Combined Heat and Power Application Tool CHP
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: tool intercomparisons exist; optimum depends on cost assumptions

tasks.name: Clean energy project screening
tasks.definition: Given a site, technology and cost inputs, estimate energy production, emissions reduction and financial viability for prefeasibility.
tasks.inputs: site climate; technology parameters; costs and incentives

open_questions: Size: 24 capabilities and 175 tasks, well over the 6-14 guidance. The domain holds ten original functions, and NAFEMS separates structural mechanics finely. Candidate merges if the editor wants fewer: material_behavior into structural_fea, renewable_energy into power_systems, fire into cfd, meshing_prepost with design_exploration.
Semiconductor process and device simulation (TCAD) solves physics, but the boundary table and the original 'ic' function put it in design. Should it move to simulate.multiphysics?
Seepage through engineered earthworks is here while natural groundwater is in earth; SVFlux and SEEP/W serve both. Confirm the line.
Human-body biomechanics (3DSSPP, Jack) is placed in simulate.multibody; ergonomic job assessment is left for operate. Confirm operate wants the assessment half.
Wind farm yield (WAsP, WindSim) solves wind flow over natural terrain; it is placed here because the output is plant energy. Earth may claim the flow model.
Industrial utility-system assessment tools (AIRMaster+, MotorMaster+, PHAST) sit in building_energy; operate may prefer them as energy management.
